- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment <0.40 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment turns neutral.
